ownership_reason: Only the gold looks up the implicit prototype and decides whether the prototype or the interfaces extended by the constructor answer; hops 1-4 hand the object type along unchanged, and the gold reads the prototype from the type itself, so no caller can change which prototype it sees. The gold's javadoc promises whether the given object type is still unknown to the type system, the predicate the facade answers; on the trigger, the prototype of interface B inherits from the unresolved interface A and is reported as known, because its implicit prototype is the built-in Object.prototype. No one-line change of the argument above the gold restores this: handing the gold the native prototype gives that prototype's own, empty interfaces, and answering native types at a hop leaves B's prototype, which is not native, unchanged. The convention is pinned outside the gold: PrototypeObjectType.getSlot (an object inherits from its implicit prototype and then from the interfaces extended by its constructor), PrototypeObjectType.toStringHelper (the walk up the implicit prototypes stops at a native object type), PrototypeObjectType.isSubtype (extended interfaces decide for interface types), with TypeCheckTest testInterfaceExtends and testBadInterfaceExtends1 and JSTypeTest testInterfaceInheritanceSubtypeChain passing; the facade's own javadoc treats the type as unknown if any of its implicit prototype properties is unknown.
